title: Portable Linux release-candidate fixtures
objective: Make Linux release-candidate fixture tests architecture-neutral so native arm64 CI validates arm64 receipts, archive names, and Rust authority while preserving the exact x64 contract

oracles: Focused Node test suite on x64 and native arm64

handoff.summary: At exact source 9c444d4e9954cf7ff2d2c133073c8ad950f7b84d, Linux release-candidate fixtures derive receipt targets, official Rust provenance, archive/checksum names, readiness markers, and installer names from the supported architecture. Literal x64 and arm64 authority ratchets remain explicit. A parent-authorized test-only archive writer lets physical Darwin exercise the complete fixture with deterministic BSD tar while production Linux retains its exact fixed GNU tar command and environment. The focused suite passes 11/11 on Linux x64, native Linux arm64, and physical Darwin arm64 with Node 26.7.0. Architecture, portable (445/445), and strict baselib gates pass on the rebased source.
risks: Darwin uses an explicit test-only BSD tar writer; both native Linux targets continue to exercise the unchanged production GNU tar path under hostile ambient PATH, TAR_OPTIONS, XZ_OPT, and umask values.
The structured target-host run objects were recorded from clean exact remote checkouts because the local parallel runner labels SSH commands with the invoking x64 host.
next_steps: Review and integrate the closure commit into the shared release baseline, then let macOS and Linux release CI repeat the same focused architecture-specific fixtures.
